title: Speed dependent descending control of freezing behavior in Drosophila melanogaster
quote: CsChrimson activation of DNp09 neurons was sufficient to trigger freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of trials
mapping_basis: Paper uses Namiki et al. 2018 name DNp09 (SS01540); kit marks the name and SS01540 ambiguous between MANC DNp09 and DNp71 (hemibrain 'DNp09'); the Namiki/Card naming used here corresponds to the MANC type of the same name, DNp09.
stimulation: 627 nm LED, 0.025 mW/mm2, 10 repetitions of 2 s on / 20 s off
sensory_condition: freely walking in 30 mm circular arena; controls raised without retinal
other_cell_types: weak off-target labeling (unspecified; paper refers to FlyLight website)
penetrance: freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of trials; freezing probability lower in flies walking fast before stimulation
n_flies_note: Fig. 6 legend: test flies with retinal n = 80, controls n = 72
notes: Freezing is the main outcome (legs coded 'no' per the stopping convention). However, the paper also reports an initial increase in walking speed ('running bout ... mostly caused by DNp09 activity') before freezing sets in, and jumps at light offset. The state of the flies at stimulus onset was not controlled in open loop, so whether this running is new rhythmic stepping in standing flies is unclear. Mated females, 4-6 days old. Expression assumed bilateral (not stated as stochastic).

title: Moonwalker Descending Neurons Mediate Visually Evoked Retreat in Drosophila
quote: Here, we present data from functional imaging, behavioral epistasis, and unilateral activation experiments that support these hypotheses.
mapping_basis: The paper's name MDN (moonwalker descending neurons) is itself a MANC type name in type_list.csv.
notes: Abstract only: the full text (cell.com open archive, ScienceDirect) returned HTTP 403 and there is no PMC copy. The supported hypotheses, stated in the preceding abstract sentence, are that 'turning while walking backward might reflect asymmetric activation of the left and right MDNs'. So unilateral MDN activation is read as producing backward walking with turning. The effector is not in the abstract; 'optogenetic' is inferred from a search-result summary of the highlights ('Optogenetic activation of LC16 or MDN cells triggers backward locomotion'), which I could not open myself. The preparation was kept as 'other' because the abstract does not show it. The abstract also describes MDN activity as 'necessary and sufficient to trigger backward walking' (citing earlier work).

title: Female contact activates male-specific interneurons that trigger stereotypic courtship behavior in Drosophila
quote: the initiation of courtship behavior is significantly correlated with the activation of the transmidline P1 interneurons, the descending P2b interneurons, or both
mapping_basis: synonyms.csv lists P2b (Kimura 2008, Kohatsu 2010) as ambiguous between pIP10 and DNxl053; the abstract gives no anatomy beyond 'descending', so I could not choose between them.
sensory_condition: male placed alone without a courting target
other_cell_types: other fru-expressing neurons in MARCM clones
notes: Abstract only: the full text (cell.com) returned 403 and there is no PMC copy. The outcome is 'initiation of courtship behavior' in solitary males; the abstract does not describe the specific acts or leg movements, so legs are not_assessed. Activation of fru neurons broadly 'induced an entire series of courtship acts'. MARCM gives stochastic expression, and clones could contain P1, P2b or both. The preparation was kept as intact_free; the abstract says males were 'placed alone', which is consistent with this. P2b could not be mapped from the abstract (pIP10 vs DNxl053), so it is UNMAPPED.

title: Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship
quote: Activation of pIP10 in isolated males elicited normal pulse trains throughout the stimulus duration of pIP10 activation, often interspersed with short bouts of sine song.
mapping_basis: pIP10 is a MANC type name in type_list.csv (one type).
stimulation: 625 nm red light, 10 s constant, intensities 0.3-42 uW/mm2, 3 repeats per intensity
sensory_condition: isolated male in 5 mm song-recording chamber
n_flies_note: not stated in legend; each intensity repeated 3 times
notes: The outcome is song (pulse song with some sine), recorded acoustically; legs and locomotion are not described. I read v1 and v2 of the preprint. In both versions the Fig. 4 legend ends at panel E, and panels H-J in Fig. 8 show a different genotype (pIP10+vPR9-SS1). The pass-1 locator 'H-I' could therefore not be confirmed, and I locate this record at Fig. 4D-E. The driver is labelled 'pIP10-GAL4' / 'pIP10>CsChrimson'; line IDs are in a supplementary table I did not read. The published version is Curr Biol 2024 (10.1016/j.cub.2024.01.015), which I did not open.
